text.p: Finnish fur auctioner Turkistuottajat Oy said in a statement on Monday its 1996-1997 profit would be below the year-ago profit due to weaker-than-forecast demand for blue fox fur.
"In the auction that started in Copenhagen today less than 30 percent of the blue fox fur offered was sold and prices were lower than in December's auction," Turkistuottajat said in a statement.
"Turkistuottajat Oy's profit will be clearly weaker than in the last financial period," the company said.
Turkistuottajat posted an 85.8 million markka profit before extraordinary items in the 13 months to August 1996.
Turkistuottajat's financial year normally runs from August 1 to July 31.
"Due to the uncertain prospects Turkistuottajat will offer less than the budgeted amount of blue fox pelts in the auction starting on February 17," it said.
